content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 03/15 21:15 UTC - Elevated 95th percentile latency for text-generation on rwd-2-xl (eu-west1). Feed: prod-ingest. Auto-ticket #INC-2026-451 created. @Jordan paging: paging rule matched (sev=2).

Jordan: I'm on it. seeing 95p ~ 1.8s -> 3.9s over last 6m. routing shows a spike to dedicated pool eu-west1-gpu-a. no obvious scaling events.

Maya: hmm okay. any recent model pushes? last deploy to rwd-2-xl was 20:40 UTC with kernel tunings.

Sam: deploybot shows a config bump earlier: `--kv-cache-split=on` to improve throughput. Rollout was canary -> 60% -> 100% at 20:55.

Jordan: thanks. initial mitigation: throttling burst set to 0.5 for rwd-2-xl traffic, and added fallback route to rwd-2-large-quant for user-facing routes. monitoring for error rate and latency.

Rachel: starting customer-impact sweep. Which customers hit the fallback? I can draft comms if needed.

Maya: quick quality check: rwd-2-large-quant has slightly different tokenization, might truncate long prompts. If we fallback, include a note about potential minor formatting differences.

Eli: hands-on keyboard for night shift. @Jordan handing off: summary -> elevated 95p latency due to kernel switch; mitigation -> route 10% to rwd-2-large-quant, throttle bursts; action items -> consider rollback of kernel flag and run a degraded canary.

Jordan: handing off to @Eli. Logs and commands below.

Jordan: ```
# routing change
redwood route update --model rwd-2-xl --fallback rwd-2-large-quant --weight 10
# throttle
redwood config set --model rwd-2-xl --burst 0.5
# rollback (if needed)
redwood deploy rollback --deploy-id deploy-2026-03-15-2040
```

Sam: statuspage draft (proposed):
StatusBot: DRAFT -> "We are investigating elevated latency for text generation in eu-west1 affecting rwd-2-xl. Some requests are being routed to a compatible model variant to maintain availability. Users may see slightly different formatting for long prompts. We will provide updates every 30 minutes until resolved."

Rachel: customer-notify draft for impacted enterprise customers: "We're investigating increased response times for text generation in eu-west1. As a temporary measure, traffic may be served by a fallback model. There is no evidence of data loss. If you rely on exact output formatting, expect minor differences. Our on-call is actively working on a rollback & quality verification. ETA for next update: 30 minutes. Contact customer-ops@redwood.ai for urgent cases."

Maya: quality checklist before full rollback: 1) run 50 synthetic prompts from high-priority promptset against rollback candidate (rwd-2-xl@v2026-03-15-2040) and fallback variant; 2) verify top-k/temperature parity; 3) quick QA sampling for hallucination/format.

Eli: immediate plan for night: keep partial fallback active, run synthetic tests, prepare rollback candidate snapshot. If synthetic tests pass and latency normalizes under 95p < 1.5s, we'll rollback kernel change to stable. If rollback not safe, extend fallback and prepare customer comms path.

Jordan: note for runbook: when doing kernel flag rollback, ensure to drain in small batches to avoid cache thrash. use `drain --concurrency=5` and monitor KV cache hit-rate.

Sam: I saw a spike in GPU mem fragmentation at 21:10 which lines up with the kernel change. Could be fragmentation interacting with burst config. Good to include in post-incident notes.

Rachel: sending customer-notify to impacted list now (internal draft); will wait 10m for update before publishing status page.

incident-bot: Reminder: create postmortem ticket and assign severity classification after mitigation. Use template: "impact, timeline, root cause, mitigations, follow-ups".

Eli: quick quality check results: 50 synthetic prompts -> average token-diff 0.7%, formatting changes in 4/50 long prompts (minor). Hallucination rates unchanged.

Eli: proceeding with cautious rollback of kernel flag on a 10% canary, monitoring. command: `redwood deploy rollback --deploy-id deploy-2026-03-15-2040 --canary 10`

Sam: canary rollback successful for 10%. 95p latency down to 1.4s on canary nodes. no error spike.

Eli: expanding rollback to 50% while monitoring KV hit-rate and CPU utilization.

Jordan: nice. when 50% stable, we can promote fully. Rachel - recommend we update customers: we have an active rollback and expect full restore in ~20-30m.

Rachel: sending update to customers now. statuspage ready to publish.

StatusBot: PUBLISHED -> "Resolved: We identified a kernel tuning change that increased latency for rwd-2-xl in eu-west1. We rolled back the change and restored normal latency. Some traffic was temporarily routed to a fallback model; there is no data loss. If you continue to see issues, contact support."

Jordan: closing notes: mitigation steps -> partial fallback + throttle -> synthetic QA -> canary rollback -> full rollback. Postmortem owners: Maya (root cause analysis), Sam (infra/fragmentation), Rachel (customer comms).

Maya: follow-ups: 1) add additional perf tests for kernel changes on staging with mem-fragmentation scenarios; 2) improve rollout gating to include KV hit-rate regression alarms; 3) craft customer-facing FAQ about fallback behavior and pinning guidance.

Rachel: draft FAQ bullet to add to KB: "If you require output parity, ask for model-pinning to a specific model id/version. Our Support team can help pin models for enterprise plans to guarantee stable behavior during rollouts."

Eli: leaving final handoff notes for morning: monitor 95p for next 2 hours, confirm no regression in embedding churn, close incident after postmortem ticket created.

Jordan: thanks team. I'll file the postmortem and link this thread. Good job. :thumbsup:
